description_en: Constructed by Princess Amarakānteśvarī, this temple stands as the southernśivālayaamong the two similar Śiva temples she built in the Paśupati area in 1856 CE (VS 1913).Located by the Bagmati River, west of the cremation site known as the Bhasmeśvara Ghāṭa, the Amarakānteśvara Mandira closely mirrors another temple to the north, recognized as the Sureśakānteśvara Mandira (PPK0523). Facing south, the temple boasts a domed roof crowned with a metal finial. Unlike Sureśakānteśvara, the finial of this Śiva temple lacks support from four serpent bodies crafted in brass. The square superstructure follows neo-classical architecture but is coated with traditionalbajraplaster, featuring a miniature dome at each of its four corners. The substructure, slightly larger than the superstructure, follows Newar-style brick architecture and serves as the sanctum of the temple. An ornate stone archway (toraṇa), adorned with a figure of Chepu, a mythical water creature, frames the entrance on all four sides. The sanctum houses aśivaliṅgasurrounded by statues of four other deities – Gaṇeśa, Durgā, Viṣṇu, and Sūrya – placed at the four corners of the inner walls following the Śivapāñcāyana concept. A west-facing stone statue of Kāmadeva is set within a small niche on the northeastern side of the temple.Amarakānteśvarī is credited with the construction of the temple in 1856 CE (VS 1913) (M. Thapā VS 2077, p. 205; Documenta Nepalica K_0192_0020). An inscription on a bell installed south of the temple indicates that Princess Amarakānteśvarī offered the bell through Captain Juddhamānasiṃha Rājabhaṇḍārī in 1856 CE (NS 976) (Ṭaṇḍana VS 2056, p. 538).After sustaining severe damage in the 2015 earthquakes, the temple underwent reconstruction by the Pashupati Area Development Trust in 2018 CE (VS 2075) (as reported by a guard at Pashupati, Lāmichāne, male, age 48). The bell, which was the only source of information regarding the temple’s construction, is no longer at the site. As of August 2023, it is yet to be reinstalled even after the completion of the temple’s reconstruction. Therefore, it remains uncertain whether it was Juddhamānasiṃha or Siddhimānasiṃha who assisted Amarakānteśvarī in offering the bell. Typically, the donor of the bell is also the individual commissioning the construction of the temple to which the bell was donated.Historically, Brahmins conducted daily worship at the temple (as per a local resident, Ācārya, male, age 50). However, all daily and periodic rituals have been discontinued since the 2015 earthquakes (as reported by a guard at Pashupati, Lāmichāne, male, age 48).
description_ne: राजकुमारी अमरकान्तेश्वरीले विसं १९१३ (सन् १८५६) मा ‌निर्माण गर्न लगाएका दुईवटा शिवालयहरूमध्ये एक यस मन्दिरको पुनर्निर्माण विसं २०७५ (सन् २०१८) मा पशुपति क्षेत्र विकास कोषले गरेको थियो ।भस्मेश्वरघाटमा चौतरिया चोकदेखि दक्षिणपट्टिको चोकमा दुईवटा शिवालयहरू बनेका छन् - अमरकान्तेश्वर र सुरेशकान्तेश्वर (PPK0523) । यो मन्दिर सुरेशकान्तेश्वरको दक्षिणतिर रहेको छ । दक्षिणाभिमुख यस मन्दिर तीनतहको वर्गाकार पेटीमाथि निर्माण गरिएको छ । गुम्बज शैलीको छानोमाथि धातुको गजुर हालिएको छ । तर संगैको सुरेशकान्तेश्वरमा जस्तै गजुरमाथि धातुका छत्र र चारवटा नागहरू भने यहाँ राखिएका छैनन् । दुई तहको यस मन्दिरको माथिल्लो भागमा सेतो बज्रलेपन गरी चार कुनामा सानो आकारका गुम्बज पनि राखिएका छन् । तल्लो भाग भने इँटा देखिने गरी बनाइएको छ । मन्दिरको चारै दिशामा छेपु आकृति कुँदिएको ढुङ्गाको तोरण सहितका ढोकाहरू रहेका छन् । तर दक्षिणतिरको ढोकालाई मूलद्वारका रूपमा लिइन्छ । गर्भगृहमा प्रमुख देवताको रूपमा शिवलिङ्ग स्थापना गरिएको छ र चार कुनामा शिव पाञ्चायन अनुसार गणेश, दुर्गा, विष्णु र सूर्यका मूर्तिहरू स्थापना गरिएका छन् । मन्दिरको उत्तरपूर्वपट्टि कामदेवको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । Pruscha (1975, p.31) ले यस शैलीको मन्दिरलाई १९औं शताब्दीको प्रसिद्ध शिव मन्दिर शैली भनेका छन् ।यो मन्दिरको स्थापना अमरकान्तेश्वरीले विसं १९१३ (सन् १८५६) मा गर्न लगाएको देखिन्छ (M. Thapā VS 2077, p.205) । मन्दिरको दक्षिणपट्टी राखिएको घण्टमा रहेको अभिलेखमा राजकुमारी अमरकान्तेश्वरीले नेसं ९७६ (सन् १८५६) मा कपतान जुद्धमान सिं राजभण्डारीमार्फत घण्ट बनाई चढाएको विवरण उल्लेख छ (Ṭaṇḍana VS 2056, p.537) । Michaels and Tandon (2017, p.70) ले भने ‘सिद्धिमान सिंह राजभण्डारीमार्फत’ भनेका छन् । हाल (सन् २०२३, अगष्ट) मन्दिर परिसर भित्र मन्दिर सम्बन्धी थप जानकारी हुने कुनै अभिलेख प्राप्त छैन । विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को भूकम्पले मन्दिरमा धेरै क्षति पुर्‍याई जीर्ण बनाएको थियो । पुरानै शैलीमा विसं २०७५ (सन् २०१८) मा पशुपति क्षेत्र विकास कोषले यसको पुनर्निर्माण गरेको थियो (guard at Pashupati, Lāmichāne, male, age 48) । तर पुनर्निर्माणको कार्य सकिए तापनि उक्त घण्टा भने अहिले (सन् २०२३, अगष्ट) सम्म राखिएको छैन । त्यसैले अमरकान्तेश्वरीले जुद्धमान सिं अथवा सिद्धिमान सिंह मध्ये कसका मार्फत घण्ट चढाएकी थिइन् भन्ने यकीन गर्न सकिएन ।विगतमा मन्दिरमा ब्राह्मणहरूद्वारा नित्यपूजा गर्ने गरिन्थ्यो (local resident, Ācārya, male, age 50) । विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) को भूकम्प देखि अहिलेसम्म यहाँ नित्यपूजा लगायत कुनै धार्मिक-सांस्कृतिक गतिविधि हुने गरेको छैन (guard at Pashupati, Lāmichāne, male, age 48) ।

historical_events.event_description: Amarakānteśvarī is credited for the construction of the temple. The inscription on a bell installed south of the temple states that Princess Amarakānteśvarī offered the bell through Captain Juddhamānasiṃha Rājabhaṇḍārī. Michaels and Tandon (2017, p.70), however, mention that she offered the bell through Siddhimānasiṃha Rājbhaṇḍārī. The bell is no longer at the site. Therefore, it could not be ascertained if it was Juddhamānasiṃha or Siddhimānasiṃha, who assisted Amarakānteśvarī in offering the bell. Usually, the donor of the bell is also the person to commission the construction of the temple the bell was donated to.
The temple was reconstructed by the Pashupati Area Development Trust after it was badly damaged in the 2015 earthquakes.
